xray.one_line: Email infrastructure for AI agents: each agent gets its own address, an API to send and receive, and hosted code that runs on every inbound message.
xray.what_it_does: Primitive (primitive.dev, also onprimitive.com for its business pitch) is email infrastructure for AI agents, a Y Combinator company founded in 2026 in San Francisco. It gives an agent a managed *.primitive.email address (or a customer's own domain), a REST API, MCP server, CLI and SDKs to send, receive and search mail, a one-line chat verb that sends a message and waits for the threaded reply, and hosted JavaScript Functions that run on every inbound message, while Primitive runs the mail servers, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, bounces and sending reputation. On top of that infrastructure it also says it deploys and operates agents for customers, starting as a general interface to the business by email. [s3, s4, s5, s6, s1, s19, s20]

situations.title: A Function on a customer inbox, holding the org's key
reach: Every inbound message to the routed address, written by anyone who can send email; Primitive applies spam and policy filtering, but the content is untrusted text
The whole organisation's stored mail, domains, Functions and Memories through the injected PRIMITIVE_API_KEY: Primitive credentials are organisation-scoped and do not advertise granular scopes
Replying, forwarding and sending as the business, from its own domain, to recipients the account's send rules allow (broader external sending is enabled per organisation)
Any external HTTP API the handler is written to call
Per-Function secrets injected into the running handler, such as a payment provider key (the docs' own example is STRIPE_KEY)
Customers and partners whose correspondence is stored until the business deletes it: Primitive does not auto-delete mail on a schedule
asked_our_example: Answer order and product questions sent to this one address, in the same thread
Read only the thread being answered; leave the rest of the organisation's mail alone
Never move money and never write to anyone who did not write first
gap: The handler's key reaches the whole organisation, not the one address it serves; there is no narrower scope to give it
Secrets and outbound HTTP make the handler able to act on payment and other systems on the strength of text that anyone can email in
Sending beyond the thread depends on the organisation's send rules, which are settings, not the mandate

situations.title: An assistant connected to the org's mail over MCP
reach: Every message in the authorised organisation: the connector acts on the whole organisation, reading and writing its email
Sending new mail and replies through the organisation's verified domains
On /mcp/full: domains, webhook endpoints and filters, which decide where inbound mail is delivered
Correspondents in the inbox, rendered inside the assistant host by the in-agent inbox widget
asked_our_example: Summarise and triage new mail for the person
Draft replies; send only after the person approves each one
Never change where mail is routed
gap: Send confirmation is a hint to the host (destructiveHint): a well-behaved assistant asks first; nothing in Primitive's grant distinguishes draft from send
Connecting /mcp/full puts routing (webhooks, filters) in reach of the same conversation that reads untrusted mail

situations.title: An agent that signs itself up for an email identity
reach: Creating a new Primitive organisation and managed inbox with one unauthenticated POST, no email and no human in the loop
Replying to anyone who has already written to the new address (reply-only, 10 sends an hour, 50 a day)
Durable Memories that keep state across turns and emails
Asking a human to confirm an email, or handing them a claim link, to upgrade the account (send cap lifts, Functions unlock)
asked_our_example: Use the email identity the operator issued; do not create accounts
Ask the operator before any external correspondence
gap: The agent can mint its own identity and inbox that the operator never issued and may not know exists until a claim is asked for
Correspondence from that identity is outside any record the operator keeps

questions: Can a Function's injected key be narrowed to the one address or route it serves, instead of the whole organisation?
When a Function or MCP assistant sends, what does the record show about which inbound message prompted it, and can a customer export that link?
Which organisations have send_to_any_domain enabled, and what review does Primitive apply before it turns that on?
How do the agents you deploy and operate for customers decide when to create a new specialised agent, and who approves it?
Would you publish the _agents authorisation result alongside each send, so a recipient can see which agent sent and under which rule?
Your security page says it describes current practice, not an audited control set: is a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audit planned, and what would it cover first?

help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Primitive's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
